column1: # Short names of the Spartans' spoken lines (vocalizations) that a Halo Infinite film carries, by the line index the
# film writes (the 12-bit `line` of a chatter message), for the builds whose line layout is known.
# WHAT A NAME IS. The game's vocalization tables name every entry by the 32-bit hash of a lowercase string, never by
# the string. The names below are those strings, found by a dictionary search and kept only when the hash of the
# string (MurmurHash3 x86 32-bit, seed 0, over the ASCII bytes) EQUALS the hash recorded for that entry of the game's
# tables. The hash is the second column: the test recomputes it from the name. A name whose words read as nonsense
# was dropped, and so was a line that two readable strings claimed.
# WHAT IS KEPT. For each entry: its index in the game's tables (first column), the recorded hash (second column) and
# the name (third column). No file of the game is reproduced and no spoken text is kept: only the maintainer's
# own result of the search. The table is not taken from libfilmshell (which names no vocalization).
# WHICH LINES. The entries 0 to 914 (first table) and 2732 to 2956 (fourth table); the other entries are not named
# because the order of the tables between them is not established. See `table.go` for the builds.
